summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a purge route that deletes a list of users.

findings.title: User delete route has no admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling routes use. The handler deletes the user named in the URL without checking who sent the request.
findings.consequence: Any caller who can reach the server can delete any user account. A caller can also walk through ids to delete every user.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET /users and POST /users/purge routes already do.
findings.suggested_change:
admin.delete("/users/:id", requireAdmin, async (req, res) => {
  await db.removeUser(req.params.id);

findings.title: Purge drops removeUser promises
findings.problem: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nothing awaits or catches the removeUser promises. db.removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled.
findings.consequence: One unknown id in a purge request causes an unhandled rejection that crashes the Node process. The response also reports every id as removed before any deletion finishes.
findings.fix: Await Promise.allSettled over the removeUser calls. Report the count of calls that succeeded.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete routes have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds two routes that delete users, and no test file exists in the repository. No test covers authorization, unknown ids or the purge count.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the missing admin check and the crash on unknown ids can ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add route tests for non-admin callers, unknown ids and the purge response count.
